steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a piece stuck. You built **Button variants** in *Thinking in Tailwind*. Now write it again from an
**empty editor**: no starter, no hints, no solution to peek at. The tests are exactly the ones you passed
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old code feels like knowing
it; rebuilding it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.title: Rebuild Button variants cold
prompt: Write `buttonClass({ variant, size, disabled })` returning the class string for a button, built from **complete** class names:
- variant `"primary"`: `"bg-blue-600 text-white hover:bg-blue-700"`; `"secondary"`: `"bg-gray-100 text-gray-900 hover:bg-gray-200"`; `"danger"`: `"bg-red-600 text-white hover:bg-red-700"`
- size `"sm"`: `"px-2 py-1 text-sm"`; `"md"` (default): `"px-4 py-2"`; `"lg"`: `"px-6 py-3 text-lg"`
Parts appear in that order, joined by single spaces. `variant` defaults to `"primary"`.
**From memory this time:** the editor starts empty and the tests are the ones you passed in the lesson.
Type the shape yourself, then fill it in:
